name: oes-command-centre
narrative: Once contracts are running, Ada's question is not where the shipments are — it is which children are about to go without, and what can still be done about it. The command centre opens by admitting the uncomfortable part: the Kano plant sends clean structured events, a despatch from Lagos arrives as a standard advice document, and the Port Sudan to El Fasher corridor — which serves the worst famine phases — arrives as a driver's phone check-in, hand-keyed and labelled as such. So the picture is brightest exactly where access is easiest. Because every milestone keeps planned, estimated and actual as three separate timestamps, lateness is a measurement rather than an argument; and because status is derived from an append-only event log, nobody can clear a red row by editing a field. Onto that Ada adds the demand side: a caseload per district, so a nine-day delay is reported as twelve thousand children missing a full course by a named date rather than as tonnage at risk. They see the shortfall a partner in Borno raised from their own screen, reallocate from a surplus warehouse in Kassala, and watch the cover, the pipeline gap and the map recompute against the decision they just recorded.

ada.name: Ada Nwosu
ada.role: Procurement and supply lead, Operation End Starvation
ada.intro: Ada is responsible for four corridors across Nigeria, Sudan, Ethiopia and Burkina Faso. Today they find out a consignment is late from a phone call, work out what to do about it in a messaging group, and record the decision nowhere. They want the exceptions ranked by the children behind them, and the response recorded against the evidence that prompted it.

slides.title: Which children are about to go without
slides.narration: Once the contracts are running, the question stops being procurement and becomes operational. A status board can tell you a consignment is nine days late. What a program director needs to know is which children go without because of it, where, and by when — and what can still be done in the time remaining. That is the difference between a screen you look at and a screen you act on, and it is what this one is built around.

slides.title: Three ways the data arrives, and the honest one
slides.narration: The data arrives three different ways, because that is the real capability gradient of this supply chain. The Kano plant emits structured visibility events to the international standard — machine to machine, no typing. The Lagos despatch arrives as an advice document, the same shipment-to-package-to-item tree the commodity trade has used for fifty years. And the Port Sudan to El Fasher leg arrives as a driver's phone check-in: a consignment number, a place, what happened. Sudan has no domestic producer and that corridor runs on paper waybills, so the lowest tier is not a fallback — it is the honest case, and it is the one serving the worst famine phases. Anything hand-keyed says so, everywhere it appears.

slides.title: Late is a measurement, not an argument
slides.narration: Every milestone on every leg keeps three separate times: what was planned, what is now estimated, and what actually happened. That sounds like bookkeeping and it is the reason a delay can be discussed at all — if the plan is overwritten each time the estimate moves, then nothing is ever late and any number can be argued away. Keeping all three means this consignment is nine days behind the plan it was awarded against, and that figure survives the conversation.

slides.title: Nobody can clear a red row by editing a field
slides.narration: The status you are looking at is not a field anybody types into. It is derived from an append-only log of what was reported, and the same is true of every actual time on every milestone. There is no cell to change before a Monday meeting. That single constraint is what makes the queue beside it worth trusting: a red row goes away when the situation changes, not when someone decides it looks bad.

slides.title: The caseload underneath the map
slides.narration: Until now the famine-phase colouring under the map has been context. Ada adds the caseload behind it — how many severely malnourished children each district is expected to have this month, and where that estimate comes from. With a denominator, delivery stops being tonnage and becomes coverage: this district is at ninety-one percent of need, this one at thirty-four, and here are the children with no carton assigned to them. Volume delivered could never distinguish a large delivery into a small caseload from a small delivery into a huge one.

slides.title: Twelve thousand children, by the ninth of September
slides.narration: Now the queue can rank by what actually matters. Every row carries the same unit — children who miss a full course of treatment — because that is the only quantity a late consignment, a short receipt, an expiring batch and a partner's shortfall all share, and ranking them against each other any other way is not an ordering. Behind each figure is what physically arrived, the rate the site is consuming it, and the date the store runs dry; expand a row and the derivation is there. Below the late consignments sits a different kind of risk: cartons sitting where the caseload is too small to work through them before they expire, which is a loss nobody is currently looking for.

slides.title: The signal came from the ground
slides.narration: This exception was not something the system worked out on its own. It was raised by the organisation running the feeding sites in Borno, from their own screen, four days ago — and it says so. That distinction matters more than it looks. A centre that invents its own alerts is running a monitoring product. A centre responding to what the people holding the cartons reported is running a coordination product, and that is the actual shape of the relationship between OES and its partners.

slides.title: Ada closes the signal the partner raised
slides.narration: Ada answers the shortfall Komadugu raised in the last scene. Eighty-seven cartons move from Gombe, which is holding well above what its own caseload can consume, to Askira, with the reason recorded. What that creates is a real consignment with planned milestones rather than a status change — so Askira's weeks of cover deliberately do NOT move yet, because cartons on the road are not cartons on a shelf, and the centre says so instead of claiming the stronger word. What does change is the signal: it closes against the action that answered it, carrying who decided and why, and the headline stops counting its eighty-seven children. The report and the decision are now one record — which is the thing a messaging group can never give you afterwards.
